page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-32xCPU-64GB is a Cloud Native family server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs, indicating a thread-per-core ratio of 1.0. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz and utilizes a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show a mix of average and strong performance across various workloads. The instance achieves strong results in Geekbench single-core (2082.0) and multi-core (17101.0) tests, as well as in bzip3 multi-threaded decompression (227.04 GB/sec) and PassMark CPU encryption (37135.43). However, stress-ng single-core CPU performance is poor, falling into the bottom 10% with a score of 787.38, while multi-core stress-ng performance is average at 19911.79. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks fall within the average range, as do Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput. Large-model LLM inference prompt processing using a 70B model is weak at 6.88 tokens/sec.

The shared CPU allocation model presents a tradeoff, as reflected in the poor single-core stress-ng results despite strong Geekbench scores. This resource density makes the instance a cost-efficient option for multi-threaded workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores continuously. It is suited for multi-threaded decompression, text processing, software compilation, and general-purpose database operations, but less optimal for single-core intensive tasks or large-scale LLM inference.
